title: Punjab Floods 2025
body: In 2025, Punjab was hit by severe floods. Very heavy monsoon rain fell not only in Punjab but also in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir, and western disturbances brought even more moisture. The Satluj, Beas, Ravi and Ghaggar were already flowing high, so the extra water from the hills and local rain made them overflow. Human factors made matters worse: old and weak river embankments (dhusi bandh) gave way, houses and farms had been built too close to the rivers, silt and mud had reduced the capacity of rivers and dams, and in some areas flood warnings came late or were unclear. Villages, paddy fields, poultry and dairy farms, roads, bridges and border fences were damaged; thousands moved to relief camps, and murky standing water spread waterborne diseases.
